terms.def: The flow of electrons through a circuit.
terms.more: Measured in amperes. In formulas it is written I. A difference in voltage is what makes it flow.

terms.def: The unit of electrical current.
terms.more: Often shortened to amp, symbol A. One ampere is 1000 milliamperes.

terms.def: The electrical push, or pressure, between two points that makes electrons flow.
terms.more: Measured in volts. In formulas it is written E. Voltage is the push; current is the flow that results.

terms.def: The unit of voltage, the electrical push.
terms.more: Symbol V. One kilovolt is 1000 volts; one microvolt is one millionth of a volt.

terms.def: The rate at which electrical energy is used.
terms.more: Measured in watts. In formulas it is written P, and P = I x E.

terms.def: The unit of electrical power.
terms.more: Symbol W. Watts = volts x amperes. One watt is 1000 milliwatts.

terms.def: The opposition to the flow of current.
terms.more: Measured in ohms and written R in formulas. It opposes direct current, alternating current and RF current alike.

terms.def: The unit of resistance and of impedance.
terms.more: Ohms = volts divided by amperes.

terms.def: The capacity to do work; in a circuit it is what the source supplies and what the parts use or store.
terms.more: Power is the rate at which energy is used. A capacitor stores energy in an electric field and an inductor stores it in a magnetic field.

terms.def: A complete path of connected parts that current can flow around.
terms.more: Parts can be connected in series (one path) or in parallel (side by side).

terms.def: A tiny negatively charged particle; moving electrons are what make up an electric current.
terms.more: Metals conduct well because they have many free electrons.

terms.def: A material that lets electric current flow through it easily.
terms.more: Metals are generally good conductors because they have many free electrons.

terms.def: A material that lets almost no electric current flow through it.
terms.more: Glass is a good electrical insulator.

terms.def: The number of times per second that an alternating current makes a complete cycle.
terms.more: Measured in hertz (Hz). Do not confuse it with wavelength, which is a distance.

terms.def: One complete swing of an alternating current: one way, then the other, back to the start.
terms.more: The number of complete cycles each second is the frequency.

terms.def: The unit of frequency; one hertz is one cycle per second.
terms.more: Written Hz, with a capital H and a small z. 1000 Hz = 1 kHz and 1,000,000 Hz = 1 MHz.

terms.def: Alternating current: current that alternates between positive and negative directions.
terms.more: Current that only goes between one direction and zero never reverses, so it is not AC. The opposition to AC is called impedance.

terms.def: Direct current: current that flows in one direction only.
terms.more: Resistance opposes DC just as it opposes AC and RF current.

terms.def: Radio frequency current: alternating current at the high frequencies used for radio.
terms.more: Resistance opposes RF current as well as ordinary AC and DC.

terms.def: A word part put in front of a unit to make it larger or smaller by a fixed factor, such as kilo for one thousand.
terms.more: Pico = one trillionth, micro = one millionth, milli = one thousandth, kilo = one thousand, mega = one million, giga = one billion.

terms.def: The metric prefix meaning one thousandth.
terms.more: Written as a small m. 1000 milliamperes = 1 ampere, and 500 milliwatts = 0.5 watts.

terms.def: The metric prefix meaning one millionth.
terms.more: One microvolt is one one-millionth of a volt. One microfarad is 1,000,000 picofarads.

terms.def: The metric prefix meaning one trillionth, which is one millionth of a millionth.
terms.more: Written as a small p. 1,000,000 picofarads = 1 microfarad.

terms.def: The metric prefix meaning one thousand.
terms.more: Written as a small k. One kilovolt is one thousand volts, and 1,500,000 hertz is 1500 kHz.

terms.def: The metric prefix meaning one million.
terms.more: Written as a capital M; a small m means milli. 1 MHz = 1000 kHz.

terms.def: The metric prefix meaning one billion.
terms.more: Written as a capital G. 1 GHz = 1000 MHz, so 2425 MHz = 2.425 GHz.

terms.def: Kilohertz: one thousand hertz.
terms.more: Written with a small k, capital H and small z. Divide hertz by 1000 to get kHz; multiply MHz by 1000 to get kHz.

terms.def: Megahertz: one million hertz.
terms.more: Written with a capital M, capital H and small z. 1 MHz = 1000 kHz, so 3.525 MHz = 3525 kHz and 28400 kHz = 28.400 MHz.

terms.def: Gigahertz: one billion hertz, or 1000 megahertz.
terms.more: Divide MHz by 1000 to get GHz: 2425 MHz = 2.425 GHz.

terms.def: One thousandth of an ampere.
terms.more: 1.5 amperes = 1500 milliamperes, and 3000 milliamperes = 3 amperes.

terms.def: One thousandth of a watt.
terms.more: Divide milliwatts by 1000 to get watts: 500 milliwatts = 0.5 watts.

terms.def: One thousand volts.
One one-millionth of a volt.
One trillionth of a farad, a very small amount of capacitance.
terms.more: 1,000,000 picofarads = 1 microfarad.

terms.def: One millionth of a farad, a common size for marking capacitors.
terms.more: 1 microfarad = 1,000,000 picofarads.

terms.def: A unit for comparing two power levels by their ratio rather than by their difference.
terms.more: Written dB. Double the power is about 3 dB, one quarter of the power is about -6 dB, and ten times the power is 10 dB.

terms.def: The ability to store energy in an electric field.
terms.more: Measured in farads. It is the property of a capacitor. Compare inductance, which stores energy in a magnetic field.

terms.def: The unit of capacitance.
terms.more: Real parts are usually marked in microfarads or picofarads. Do not confuse it with the henry, the unit of inductance.

terms.def: The ability to store energy in a magnetic field.
terms.more: Measured in henrys. It is the property of an inductor (a coil). Compare capacitance, which stores energy in an electric field.

terms.def: The unit of inductance.
terms.more: Do not confuse it with hertz (frequency) or the farad (capacitance).

terms.def: The region of electrical force around charged objects, such as between the two plates of a capacitor.
terms.more: Capacitance is the ability to store energy in an electric field.

terms.def: The region of magnetic force around a magnet or around a wire carrying current.
terms.more: Inductance is the ability to store energy in a magnetic field.

terms.def: The opposition to AC current flow.
terms.more: Measured in ohms, the same unit as resistance.

terms.def: The rule that power equals current multiplied by voltage: P = I x E.
terms.more: Watts = amperes x volts. 13.8 V x 10 A = 138 W. Rearranged for current: I = P / E, so 120 W / 12 V = 10 A.

terms.def: The rule linking voltage (E), current (I) and resistance (R) in a circuit: E = I x R.
terms.more: Three forms: E = I x R, I = E / R and R = E / I. Use volts, amperes and ohms. Example: 90 volts / 3 amperes = 30 ohms.

terms.def: A circuit whose parts are joined end to end in a single path.
terms.more: The current is always the same through all components. In a parallel circuit it is the voltage that is the same.

terms.def: A circuit whose parts are connected side by side across the same two points.
terms.more: The voltage is always the same across all components. In a series circuit it is the current that is the same.
